title: Microsoft Teams: Conditional Access policies for selected meetings
summary: Hold: the policy control starts inside a policy without explaining how to reach it, and its Graph reference does not document authentication-context targeting in the stated API version. The page also overstates guest lockout and treats disabling enforcement as a documented way to hide the organiser's selection; the roadmap and Message Center schedules are reported accurately.

claims.claim: Publish to apps advertises a context and makes it available for assignment to downstream resources.

claims.fix: Prepend the missing navigation and policy selection: 'Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > policy > Assignments > Target resources > Select what this policy applies to > Authentication context'. The existing Target resources citation documents the in-policy portion; https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance documents reaching Policies.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies is the documented automation equivalent for creating a policy targeting an authentication context.
claims.quote: Searched: includeAuthenticationContextClassReferences v1.0 conditionalAccessPolicy. Read create-policy and conditionalAccessApplications in v1.0 and beta: v1.0 documents generic creation, while the authentication-context targeting property is documented in beta.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies with body <conditionalAccessPolicy JSON including conditions.applications.includeAuthenticationContextClassReferences: [<context id>], user assignments and grant controls>'. Link https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-post-policies?view=graph-rest-beta and state that this is beta, subject to change and not supported for production applications. The property is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/conditionalaccessapplications?view=graph-rest-beta. Do not present the bare v1.0 endpoint as a complete context-targeting operation.

claims.claim: No Microsoft page confirms that Teams meetings honour authentication-context Conditional Access policies.

claims.fix: Delete ', but no Microsoft page read confirms Teams meetings honour them' from the note. The cited Teams reference describes that integration, with its already-reported qualification that the setting currently has no effect.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Setting ConditionalAccessAttendeeVerification to false prevents organisers from seeing or selecting a context.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams ConditionalAccessAttendeeVerification admin center; Teams meetings ConditionalAccessAttendeeVerification authentication context meeting options. Read Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy: false is described as disabling enforcement, not hiding or preventing selection.
claims.fix: Change controls[3].governs to 'Whether authentication contexts are enforced for meetings organised by users under a meeting policy'. Replace the false-setting advice with 'Set ConditionalAccessAttendeeVerification to False on policies where authentication-context enforcement should be disabled.' In Governance controls replace 'the meeting policy must allow organisers to select it' with 'the meeting policy must enable authentication-context enforcement'. Do not promise that False removes the organiser's selection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Publishing an authentication context without assigning a Conditional Access policy supplies no additional policy requirement.
claims.quote: If no Conditional Access policy is assigned to an ACRS value the claim might still be issued, because all policy requirements are satisfied.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/developer-guide-conditional-access-authentication-context for the statement about contexts with no assigned policy.

claims.claim: A context demanding a compliant device will stop guests and unmanaged devices joining the meeting.
claims.quote: However, you can use device trust settings to unblock external users while still requiring managed devices.
claims.fix: Replace 'a context that demands a compliant device will stop guests and unmanaged devices joining that meeting' with 'participants who lack the required claims are prompted to retry obtaining a token or join the lobby if enabled'. This is the documented Teams behaviour; guest status alone is not proof of failure.
